Alex Kim: Heads up — noticed a decode-batching regression when tool/function calls include structured output + stop tokens. p99 spikes from ~90ms -> ~320ms for chat workloads.
Morgan Li: ugh. any quick repro/data?
Alex Kim: repro on canary with a 10% sample of chat traffic. Key pattern: toolcall requests often cause `pause_for_tool()` and the batch stalls waiting on I/O, but batch formation still tries to pack other requests which then hit stop-token handling logic and slow down kernel selection.
Sam Ortiz: do we have profiler traces? where is time going — GPU kernels or queue wait?
Alex Kim: flamegraph attached in thread (summary inline): ~60% time spent in `decode_loop->handle_tool_pause` (CPU spin/wait), ~20% in kernel selection path (`select_kernel_for_seq_len`), ~15% in memcpy/KV handling, rest in waiting for tool service.
Jen Park: that suggests queue policy is allowing batches with mixed toolcall/non-toolcall. maybe we should segregate toolcall ops from normal decode batches.
Alex Kim: exactly. current continuous batching heuristics: FIFO with soft token budget per-batch. We saw KV cache hit rate drop from 0.82 -> 0.55 for affected sessions (context switches when paused). Also avg batch size dropped 12 -> 6.
Morgan Li: propose quick experiments:
- A: mark incoming requests that will invoke tools as non-batchable (no background batching)
- B: allow preemption: if a batch contains a toolcall, flush after N tokens or after timeout T_short
- C: change queue_policy -> `priority_by_tool_flag` so tool-free requests can bypass paused batches
Sam Ortiz: sounds good. any perf targets? what should we tune?
Alex Kim: target: restore p99 <= 120ms and batch size >= 10 for non-tool requests. token budget targets: global per-device budget 4096, per-batch soft 512, per-request soft 128 seems OK but toolcalls often emit 200+ tokens during function output.
Jen Park: I think we also need to tweak stop-token handling: right now we run stop-token checks in the decode hot path which forces kernel changes when a structured output is expected. Maybe move a light pre-scan that flags streams and selects a compatible kernel up-front.
Morgan Li: can you sketch config we can flip in canary? I can deploy.
Alex Kim: sample config to try:

```
continuous_batching:
  max_device_token_budget: "4096"
  per_batch_soft_token_limit: "512"
  per_request_soft_token_limit: "128"
  toolcall_batching: "segregate"   # options: segregate | allow_preempt
  allow_tool_preempt: "true"
  queue_policy: "priority_by_tool_flag"
  stop_token_mode: "pre_scan"      # options: inline_check | pre_scan
  pre_scan_limit: "8"              # tokens to inspect for structured markers
```

Sam Ortiz: Nice. For metrics, add counters: `batches_with_toolcalls`, `avg_wait_ms_tool_batches`, `kv_cache_hit_by_batch_type`.
perf-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: infra/canary/1769004400 -> eng-runtime (rolling 5%).
Jen Park: I'll own experiment A and metrics. @Morgan can you do canary deploy? @Sam will capture traces.
Morgan Li: on it, deploying now. will post roll status.
perf-bot: Deploy started. commit: 3f9a8b2. Canary target: 5%.
Morgan Li: canary up. initial results (10m): p50/p95/p99 non-tool requests: 42ms / 98ms / 118ms. tool-invoking requests p99 still ~300ms but tool-free improved.
Alex Kim: progress. upload detailed trace afterwards but early win for segregating toolcalls. next steps: if preempt helps more, flip to `allow_preempt` and test.
Sam Ortiz: also want to try kernel selection tweak: when `pre_scan` sees structured output, pick attention kernel variant optimized for frequent stop tokens (less branching). I'll add a microbench.
Jen Park: assign: Sam -> kernel microbench, Alex -> pre_scan implementation (cheap, avoid copying tokens), Morgan -> canary ops and metrics, me -> analyze KV hit changes.
Alex Kim: created a tiny checklist in thread: 1) flip toolcall_batching to segregate (done) 2) add metrics (Sam) 3) implement pre_scan prototype (Alex) 4) microbench kernel (Sam) 5) run 3-day canary if numbers hold.
Morgan Li: noted. thanks team :rocket:
Sam Ortiz: quick note — we should avoid marking all toolcalls non-batchable; high-frequency tiny toolcalls (<=16 tokens) could still be batched. add `toolcall_batch_decision_threshold`.
Alex Kim: good call. add `toolcall_batch_decision_threshold: 16` to config.
perf-bot: Canary report (10m): success rate 100%, no crashes.
Jen Park: cool. we'll reconvene after 24h metrics. if p99 stays under target we can promote change to stable and add a rollout plan for Dedicated clusters.
Morgan Li: logging full traces to s3://redwood-perf/toolcall-batching/1769004321/ for postmortem.
Alex Kim: thanks all — huge win so far. follow-ups in PRs.
